# Code of conduct

EXDA is built and used by researchers, engineers and students. We want taking
part — reporting a bug, asking a question, contributing code — to be a good
experience for everyone, whatever their background, experience or identity.

## Expected

- Be respectful and constructive, also when you disagree.
- Assume good intent; ask before concluding.
- Give credit, and accept feedback on your own work gracefully.
- Respect confidentiality: do not post other people's or partners' data,
  names or unpublished results.

## Not acceptable

- Harassment, insults, or discriminatory or demeaning remarks.
- Personal or political attacks, trolling.
- Publishing other people's private information without their permission.
- Any other conduct that would be inappropriate in a professional setting.

## Reporting

All contact goes through GitHub; there is no public email address.

- For abusive content, use GitHub's **Report content** option (the `…` menu on
  any comment or issue). GitHub's own staff review these reports.
- To reach the maintainer about a concern, open a short issue titled
  **"Code of conduct: please contact me"** *without any details*. The
  maintainer will follow up with you privately.

Reports are handled confidentially, and nobody is penalised for reporting in
good faith.

## Consequences

The maintainer may edit or remove comments, issues and contributions that
break this code, and may block people who repeatedly or seriously break it.

## Scope and attribution

This code applies in the EXDA repository and wherever someone represents the
project. It is adapted from the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), version 2.1.
